habitat: Widely cultivated across India as an ornamental hedge and garden climber
ecological_importance: Provides dense nesting cover for small birds and lizards. Papery bracts protect the minute true flowers from intense sunlight.
conservation_status: Not Evaluated / Widely Naturalized and Cultivated
threats: None; invasive in certain tropical island ecosystems, but managed as an ornamental in urban settings.
conservation_actions: Maintained and pruned as landscape hedging on campus.
field_identification_notes: Scrambling woody shrub/vine with sharp, curved axillary thorns.
Brilliant papery bracts (magenta, pink, purple) surrounding tiny white flowers.
ml_relevance: Vibrant papery bracts and sharp axillary thorns provide distinctive visual classification features.

ar_information.quick_identification: Thorny scrambling vine; large papery colored bracts; tiny white tubular flowers.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Resilient drought-tolerant hedge providing dense avian nesting cover.
ar_information.conservation_message: Secure / Widely Cultivated. The colorful parts that look like petals are actually modified leaves called bracts; the true flower is the tiny white tubular structure in the center.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Campus boundary walls, gates, and ornamental garden trellises
